data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Ghareebah means 'Stranger' or 'Foreigner'. This name is derived from the root 'G-H-R' which signifies 'strangeness' or 'otherness'. In Islamic spirituality, the term can also symbolize a seeker of truth, someone who is different yet remains steadfast in their beliefs. The name Ghareebah carries the meaning “Stranger, Foreigner” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghareebah usually hope their child will grow to embody stranger, foreigner and live with faith, good character and purpose.
